name: Investigating Aesthetic Transfer in Generative Models for Architectural Design (pilot)
description: A Pilot Study on Consensus-Based Fine-Tuning and Human Evaluation. Consensus-based aesthetic evaluation of a corpus of 300 architectural works (Wikimedia Commons), fine-tuning of a generative image model on the photographs selected by the consensus, and blind human evaluation of the generated images.
researchQuestion: Is there a shared aesthetic judgement of architecture, and how much of it can a generative image model absorb and transfer into the architectural designs it generates when fine-tuned on photographs selected by consensus? The pilot study measures: (1) the consensus among raters; (2) the aesthetic transfer, comparing images from the model fine-tuned on the preferred photographs (AESTHETIC) with those from the model fine-tuned on randomly chosen photographs (CONTROL) and from the starting model (BASE), through blind ratings and pairwise choices; (3) whether the raters who built the consensus recognise it in the generated images; (4) the reliability of human evaluation; (5) the sample size needed for a full study.
hypothesis: Exploratory pilot study: it does not test a single hypothesis but estimates effects with their uncertainty. Starting expectation: if fine-tuning transfers the aesthetic judgement of the consensus, AESTHETIC images should be rated higher than CONTROL images and preferred in pairwise choices, with a stronger effect among phase-1 participants. A difference below 0.3 points on the 1–7 scale is considered negligible. The results serve to estimate the effect size and to design a full study.
